questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The type of isomerism present in nitropentammine chromium (III) chloride is
questions.solution:
The chemical formula of nitropenta ammine chromium(III) chloride is:
$\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$
It can exist in following two structures
$\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$ and
Pentaamminenitrochromium (III) chloride
$\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5 \mathrm{ONO}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$
Pentaamminenitritochromium (III) chloride
Therefore, the type of isomerism found in this compound is linkage isomerism as $\mathrm{NO}_2$ group is linked through N as $-\mathrm{NO}_2$ or through O as ONO.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify, from the following, the diamagnetic, tetrahedral complex
questions.solution: (a) Ni in $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{Cl})_4\right]^{2-}$ exist as $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ion. Cl is a weak field ligand (high spin). It will not cause pairing of electrons. Hence, configuration of $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{Cl})_4\right]^{2-}$ is Tetrahedral with two unpaired electrons (i.e., paramagnetic) and has $s p^3$ hybridisation. (b) In $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)_3\right]^{3-},\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)_3^{2-}$ is a bidentate ligand thus, give octahedral structure. (c) In $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}$, Ni exist as $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ion. $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand (low spin). Causes pairing of electrons of $3 d$ orbital. Hence, the structure of is square planar and it is diamagnetic. (d) In $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4\right]$, Ni has zero oxidation state. i.e., CO is a strong field ligand causes rearrangement and pairing of electrons of $3 d$ and $4 s$ orbital. Structure of $\mathrm{Ni} \left(\mathrm{CO}_4\right)$ is tetrahedral with $ s p³$ hybridisation and it is diamagnetic. Hence, (4) is the correct answer.$$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct order for the wavelength if absorption in the visible region.
questions.solution:
When central metal ion is same (here ${Ni}^{2 +}$ ), the absorption of colour depends on the ligand.

According to spectrochemical series, various ligands are as follows

$I < {Br}^{-} < {Cl}^{-} < {NO}_{3}^{-} < F^{-} < {H}_{2}O$

$< {NH}_{3} < {NO}_{2}^{-} < {CN}^{-} < CO$

Thus, ${H}_{2}O$~is the weakest ligand among these, therefore the absorbed energy will be lowest in
$\left[Ni\left({H}_{2}O\right)6\right]2 +,$ so it will absorb highest wavelength (red light).

$E ∝ \dfrac{1}{λ}$

$∴$~The order of increasing wavelength is

$\left[Ni\left({NO}_{2}\right)6\right]4 - < \left[Ni\left({NH}_{3}\right)6\right]2 + < \left[Ni\left({H}_{2}O\right)6\right]2 +$
